causal_change.factor: Admissibility proof scope for a representation-changing fixed causal-edge carrier
causal_change.before: At the first fixed edge with no identity-preserving handoff and one source-grounded deterministic reconstruction, the transport compiler may admit a relational bridge from a reachable-domain condition showing that the reconstruction satisfies the consumer predicate. The proof can remain specific to the witnessed reachable subdomain and need not show that reconstruction preserves every producer-state distinction required by the downstream predicate and freshness obligation across the edge's full source-declared value domain.
causal_change.after: At that same first fixed heterogeneous edge, with the same endpoints, representations, reconstruction, predicates, freshness rule, authority, and single-bridge limit, the compiler admits the relational bridge only when one source-grounded predicate-quotient certificate proves that every producer state allowed by the edge's existing type invariants and direct control guards maps to a consumer state satisfying the unchanged downstream predicate, and that no two producer states collapsed by reconstruction differ on any fact required by that predicate or freshness rule. If this domain-total obligation cannot be proved from existing source facts, the edge remains one open relational-transport obligation and no bridge is emitted.
causal_change.why_causal: Whether a lossy reconstruction is a valid causal carrier depends on sufficiency for the downstream obligation over the states the fixed edge can admit, not merely on deterministic execution along one reproduced trace. Replacing witnessed-subdomain admissibility with predicate-quotient sufficiency directly determines whether the final producer receives a sound bridge or an explicit missing handoff. The witness, preimage nodes and edges, first-edge trigger, bridge cardinality, endpoint sites and representations, reconstruction relation, dependency order, lifecycle scope, source authority, candidate lineage, and final engine count remain fixed; the certificate and fail-open-to-obligation outcome are necessary manifestations of this one proof-scope factor.

hypothesis.expected_effect: The sole final producer should receive relational transport only when the anchor's existing reconstruction is sufficient for the fixed consumer obligation throughout the edge's source-declared value domain. Deterministic but lossy relations that discard an obligation-relevant or freshness-relevant distinction should remain explicit open handoffs, while genuinely sufficient heterogeneous relations should retain both native representations. This should reduce unsound bridge realization, stale-state behavior, and wasted implementation effort without weakening the promoted outcome-first causal discipline. Under the frozen matched protocol this predicts zero invalid accepted arms, candidate wins strictly exceeding losses, and candidate-median Elo strictly above incumbent-median Elo.
hypothesis.falsifier: Falsify the proposal unless the frozen matched batch completes three valid pairs with zero invalid accepted arms, candidate wins strictly exceeding losses, and candidate-median Elo strictly above incumbent-median Elo. Mechanistically falsify it if a quotient certificate admits two source-allowed producer states that reconstruction collapses while they differ on an obligation-relevant or freshness-relevant fact; derives its domain from benchmark cases, generated samples, speculative representations, or an expanded lifecycle closure; changes the terminal witness, fixed preimage, endpoints, reconstruction, first-edge trigger, or one-bridge limit; authors source before the final call; or yields more than one engine lineage or artifact.
hypothesis.behavioral_novelty: Before any candidate source exists, the loop can now distinguish an existing deterministic representation change from a causally sufficient representation change. For exactly the first qualifying heterogeneous fixed edge, it forms the reconstruction-induced quotient over the source-declared producer domain and requires the unchanged downstream predicate and freshness obligation to be constant on every collapsed class. The promoted champion can record a reachable-domain relational proof, but it cannot require this domain-total quotient sufficiency or deterministically fall back to OPEN_RELATIONAL_TRANSPORT_OBLIGATION when an obligation-relevant distinction is lost.
strengths: Directly refines the promoted champion's declared lossy-reconstruction and out-of-domain freshness risks while retaining every supported upstream and final-production mechanism.
Treats representation loss by semantic sufficiency for one fixed obligation, which generalizes to compilers, services, caches, agents, data pipelines, and stateful search systems.
Uses existing static source facts and one deterministic certificate, with no probes, samples, competing relations, rankings, replicated agents, alternative candidates, or best-of-N selection.
Adds no runtime call and preserves one non-authoring contract path followed by exactly one whole-engine-producing call and artifact.
risks: An over-approximated source-declared producer domain may reject a relation that is sound on all actually reachable states.
Incomplete type invariants or control guards may force an open handoff even when a stronger source proof exists but is difficult to recover.
The quotient certificate can consume context that the final producer would otherwise use for implementation details.
A syntactically plausible sufficiency argument may still miss an implicit downstream dependency not represented in the fixed preimage.
